problem: The round's stated spend counts one dispatch per surviving raw file, and the save helpers drop the usage of a dispatch whose file already exists. saveTimedOutPartial (used by the empty-reply exit and the timeout exit) writes to `<target>.partial` whenever the target holds any text, including an earlier empty placeholder, and no reader loads a .partial; the success path (saveChildResult) overwrites the target. So a re-dispatch to the same save_result_to path (which the empty-reply advice itself prescribes) erases the paid first attempt, and a second empty reply records its usage only in the unread .partial. The empty-reply tool output also says nothing when the record went to .partial (it notes only an error), unlike the timeout exit.
impact: Token spend in research.json and report.md is a lower bound that still reads as complete (complete: true, unknown: 0) after any retry to the same raw path, so the flow-460 H outcome 'every dispatch's token use lands in the package' does not hold for retried dispatches.
suggested_fix: Keep the earlier KERYX_USAGE line when the target exists (or write each attempt to its own raw name), or have the ledger read `<raw>.partial` usage; state the .partial destination in the empty-reply output as the timeout exit does. Otherwise say in the report that retried dispatches are not counted.
evidence: spawn-subagent-tool.ts:329-333 saveTimedOutPartial picks `${abs}.partial` when existing.trim() !== ""; :2328 writes the empty placeholder through it; :2369 saveChildResult overwrites abs; the ledger loads raw/*.txt only (ledger.ts rawUsage over raws).

problem: reviewPackagePaths is run over `call.arguments`, which is JSON text. A Windows path in a command is JSON-escaped there (C:\\w\\.metaproject\\reviews\\r9): after `.metaproject` comes a backslash pair, so text.startsWith(REVIEWS, sep + 1) sees a backslash and the occurrence is skipped. The unit test passes the raw string with single backslashes, which a tool call never carries. The old regex had the same single-separator limit, so this is not a regression, but the new tracker is documented as covering both separators.
impact: On Windows a package named by path in a keryx review command is never recorded as named, so a review opened in an earlier session is not recognised and the gate falls back to the placeholder.
suggested_fix: Accept one or two separators (or JSON-decode the arguments' string values before scanning) and add a test that feeds a JSON.stringify'd Windows command.
evidence: completion-gate.ts:74; completion-gate.test.ts 'package path matching is linear' asserts only the unescaped Windows string; reviewCall() builds arguments with JSON.stringify.

problem: A pointer wins when it was written after THIS session started, whoever wrote it. The active-review pointer is one file per project root, and several sessions share a checkout. A concurrent session that runs `keryx review start` after this one began makes its pointer fresh here, so pickPackage returns that session's package even though this session's own commands name a different one; if that other review then closes, best.mtime < closedAt releases this session's gate too. Flow 460 C (nudge pointing at another PR's package) is fixed for an older pointer and left open for a newer foreign one.
impact: A session reviewing PR A is nudged about, and finally stopped on, PR B's package when a second session in the same checkout starts B.
suggested_fix: Prefer a package this session's commands name (packageDirs / reviewIds / commands) over a merely fresh pointer, and use the pointer as a tie-breaker only when this session named none.
evidence: completion-gate.ts:279-282 returns the pointer's package once fresh; namedBySession is consulted only when the pointer is NOT fresh.

problem: Two doc comments are stacked: `/** How a finding's line was arrived at. */` (line 62) sits directly above LocateMethod's own block, and LocatorRecord, the type that sentence describes, has none. Round 1 raised the same stacking (review-clean-code-w3:CC-2); the diff moved the orphan rather than removing it.
impact: Tooling shows only the nearer comment, so the orphaned sentence documents nothing.
suggested_fix: Delete line 62, or move it above `export type LocatorRecord`.
evidence: locate.ts:62-67 and :69.

problem: unreadableInputClaim is anchored now, which removes the round-1 false positives, but it still decides by free text in both directions. False positive: a sentence that opens with the input name and a reading verb about defect prose, for example 'The schema could not be loaded when the path has spaces.' or 'The payload was not found; ...' in a review of loader code, matches pattern 2 (OWN_STATEMENT accepts any sentence start). False negative: the real statement 'I could not read .metaproject/reviews/x/pr-context.json' names a path before the input, and INPUT_NAMED allows only an article and the bare name, so a starved reviewer is not caught.
impact: A finished review of schema or payload loading code is held incomplete and costs a re-dispatch (recoverable); a reviewer that really could not read its input and names a path is counted as covering its slices.
suggested_fix: Prefer a structured signal (status, needs_context, a required inputs_read field) over prose; if prose stays, allow an optional path token before the input name and require the first-person subject for pattern 2.
evidence: ledger.ts:20-36; ledger.test.ts:1171-1176 pins only the four phrasings and one defect-prose case.

title: Whole tool-call arguments retained and rescanned per stale package
problem: The tracker keeps the full arguments string of the last 64 `keryx review` calls, and namedBySession (completion-gate.ts:217) runs namesToken (an indexOf loop) over every one of them, for each review id of each stale open package scanRoot meets (:252), on every gate evaluation. Argument length is not bounded: a call that inlines a report or findings JSON is hundreds of KB.
impact: Failure mode: a checkout with ~100 stale open drafts, 64 retained calls of ~100 KB and two ids per package scans on the order of 1 GB per stop, up to 20 continues plus stalls, on the event loop of the shell; memory holds up to ~6 MB of argument text for the session. Small for ordinary short calls; it grows with the stale-draft count and argument size.
suggested_fix: At scan time keep, per call, the Set of id-shaped tokens (split on the id boundary class, capped, e.g. 256 tokens of at most 120 chars) instead of the string, and make namedBySession a Set lookup.
evidence: completion-gate.ts:161 stores call.arguments whole; :211-220 namedBySession; :252 called per stale open package; :203-208 namesToken.

title: A compaction forgets which packages the session named
problem: agent.ts rewrites the history in place on compaction (history.splice(0, history.length, ...compacted.context) at agent.ts:2997, 3625, 3992). The next update() sees a shorter history or a different last message, resets, and rescans only the compacted context, so a package named only by an earlier, now-dropped `keryx review` call is no longer named. sessionStartedAt(history) is also taken from the first remaining message.
impact: Failure mode: in a long review session that compacted after the last write to its package manifest (or after a resumed review's pointer predates the new `since`), the gate stops finding the package (completion-gate.ts:252, :280) and nudges with NO_PACKAGE_BLOCKER ('no package this session opened or named') for up to 20 continues, sending the model to run `keryx review start` or name the package again. Settle: whether the compacted context keeps the first `keryx review` call or a summary naming the id.
suggested_fix: Keep the named sets across a reset (clear only the cursor, or merge the previous sets into the rebuilt ones), and bound them by the existing caps; derive `since` from the session start recorded outside the history.
evidence: completion-gate.ts:137-156 reset() clears roots, packageDirs, reviewIds and commands; agent.ts:2997 history.splice(0, history.length, ...compacted.context).

quote: /** How a finding's `line` was arrived at. */
title: Orphaned doc comment above LocateMethod
problem: The doc comment describing how `line` was arrived at is stacked on top of the new LocateMethod JSDoc and no longer sits above LocatorRecord, which it described. Prior finding review-clean-code-w3:CC-2, still present.
impact: Reads as documentation of LocateMethod twice and leaves LocatorRecord undocumented; no runtime effect.
suggested_fix: Delete line 62 and put the sentence above `export type LocatorRecord`.
evidence: locate.ts:62-69.

problem: The empty-reply and timeout exits now write a placeholder plus KERYX_USAGE line into save_result_to. saveTimedOutPartial treats any non-blank file as a complete earlier result, so the placeholder blocks later saves: the advised re-dispatch (the output says 're-dispatch it once') that then times out with real partial text writes it to <target>.partial, which no raw reader picks up. Conversely, a re-dispatch that completes goes through saveChildResult, which overwrites unconditionally, so the first (empty) dispatch's recorded tokens are gone.
impact: Failure mode at the first retry of any empty child (a rate-limited or flaky provider under a wide wave): the retried dispatch's partial findings or the first dispatch's tokens are lost, so the round's usage total understates spend, which is what flow 460 H adds the record to state. Before this change a timed-out retry saved its partial to the target.
suggested_fix: Treat a file that holds only the placeholder (isEmptyOutput) as blank in saveTimedOutPartial, so a partial replaces it. When a write replaces a file holding a usage line, sum the earlier usage into the new KERYX_USAGE line so retried dispatches add up. The stopped-with-no-text exit (status not Completed, no text) saves the placeholder through saveChildResult over a complete earlier result; route it through the same guard.
evidence: spawn-subagent-tool.ts: saveTimedOutPartial (existing.trim() === ""); the empty exit saves NO_TEXT_PLACEHOLDER via saveTimedOutPartial; the normal exit calls saveChildResult(saveTarget.abs, `${raw}${usageSuffix()}`), which overwrites. Test 'flow 460 E/H' only covers a complete DONE result already there, not an earlier placeholder.

class_scope.enumeration_method: read every writer of save_result_to in the file: saveChildResult callers (normal exit) and saveTimedOutPartial callers (timeout exit, empty exit)

problem: namedBySession re-scans the full text of every retained command for every stale open package, on every stop. The tracker keeps whole tool-call argument strings (up to 64) and only the count is capped, not their size.
impact: Failure mode: per-stop CPU stall in the keryx shell. A session that ran 64 `keryx review ingest`-style commands with inline reports of ~1 MB, in a checkout carrying ~50 stale open drafts (the case the comment names), does 50 x 2 ids x 64 x 1 MB, about 6 GB of indexOf scanning per model stop, on the event loop, plus the memory for the retained strings. Realistic argument sizes (KBs) make it negligible, so this is a bound that is missing, not a measured stall.
suggested_fix: When the tracker scans a call, extract only the review-id tokens it names (SAFE_REVIEW_ID-shaped words next to `keryx review`) into a capped Set and test membership; or truncate the stored arguments to a few KB. Then namedBySession is O(ids).
evidence: completion-gate.ts remember(this.commands, call.arguments, MAX_SESSION_REVIEW_COMMANDS) stores the whole argument string; scanRoot calls namedBySession for each open package older than the session.

problem: The light-round recheck now runs git through defaultGitRunner, which spawns with no timeout and no kill signal, unlike gitTopLevel and gitDiffAt (15 s, SIGKILL). The result goes through processCache, which stores the pending promise and removes it only after it settles.
impact: Failure mode: if one `git merge-base` hangs (stalled network or FUSE file system, wedged git), the promise never settles and stays cached under that key. Every later readiness, complete and panel refresh in the same process awaits the same hung promise, so the gate and panel freeze until the process restarts. The other git calls in this path would fail after 15 s and be retried.
suggested_fix: Give defaultGitRunner (or the resolveBase call here) the same timeout and killSignal as gitDiffAt, and have processCache drop an entry that has not settled after a deadline.
evidence: coverage.ts spawns gitTopLevel/gitDiffAt with `timeout: 15_000, killSignal: "SIGKILL"`; prior-round.ts defaultGitRunner spawns with `stdout: "pipe", stderr: "ignore"` only.

title: partitionRegionsByFix is quadratic in region length
problem: For every context line of a mixed region the loop re-filters and re-scans changedAt (O(changes) each), and every line also runs hunks.some(...) in the kinds map. Cost is O(lines x changes) per region. Failure mode: a delta round whose scoped region is a very large mixed fix/new block (a regenerated or moved file, ~20k lines with thousands of changes) costs on the order of 1e8 operations on the single-threaded CLI/shell process, stalling it (including an in-process keryx shell) for seconds. Regions are normally small, so this is a minor tuning cost, not a defect at ordinary sizes.
evidence: slice-06 round-split.ts partitionRegionsByFix: const before = changedAt.filter((at) => at < index).at(-1); const after = changedAt.find((at) => at > index); inside the per-line loop.
suggested_fix: Precompute previous/next changed index with two linear passes, and index fix hunks by file so hunks.some is not a full scan per line.

problem: saveTimedOutPartial now also saves the empty-reply record (line 2328) and the no-text timeout record (line 2260). It counts any non-blank file at the target as a complete result. But the file a previous empty dispatch left there, `(subagent produced no text)` plus a KERYX_USAGE line, is non-blank, and every raw reader treats it as empty (RawFile.empty, ledger.ts:74). Trigger: a read_only reviewer ends empty. The tool's own advice (line 2334) says to re-dispatch it once. If that retry also ends empty, or times out after writing part of a review, its text and its usage line go to `<target>.partial`, which no raw-result reader picks up (the docstring at 325-328).
impact: The retry's partial review text never reaches the ledger or retry-eval, and its token spend is not counted. The ledger sees one empty dispatch where two ran, and that one is the stale placeholder. The round's stated spend undercounts silently, and the retry's partial findings are lost to the ledger.
suggested_fix: In saveTimedOutPartial, treat the target as free when its body without the usage line is empty or is the placeholder. Use the same test the readers apply, e.g. `isEmptyOutput(splitUsage(existing).body)`. Then overwrite it. Add a spawn test where an empty dispatch is followed by a timed-out one with text, and assert that the text lands at the target path.
evidence: spawn-subagent-tool.ts:329-334 (`existing.trim() === ""`), :2260 and :2328 (callers that write the placeholder), :2334 (advice to re-dispatch once); src/review/ledger.ts:74 (`empty` covers the placeholder).

problem: The new scope-B closure falls back to matching on (reviewer, bare raw id). The reviewer is the role name (`review-logic`), not the raw stem, so one reviewer's waves share it. When canonical findings use bare ids, ingest records the screened finding as {id: "F-001", reviewer: "review-logic"} (managed.ts:690). Then a different wave's raw F-001 also matches: wave 3's `review-logic-w3:F-001` and wave 4's `review-logic-w4:F-001` are both F-001 from `review-logic`, as the prior round's own findings.json shows. That second obligation closes `out-of-scope`, citing a screen that screened another finding.
impact: A raw finding nobody reconciled closes silently, and the ledger can report READY with it unanswered. Only bare-id canonical findings are affected. The `<raw stem>:<id>` form matches through `entry.id === oid` exactly.
suggested_fix: Record the raw stem (or the obligation id) on each IngestScreened entry, and match only on `oid`. Failing that, use the (reviewer, fid) fallback only when that reviewer has a single raw file. The pre-existing canonicalByReviewer/absorbedInto (ledger.ts:597-602) has the same cross-wave identity and should be narrowed the same way.
evidence: ledger.ts:612-613 screenedAs; ledger.ts:599-602 canonicalByReviewer (same reviewer+id identity); managed.ts:686-691 screenedRecord stores the canonical id and reviewer; the prior findings.json holds review-logic-w3:F-001 and review-logic-w4:F-001, both reviewer=review-logic.

problem: The narrowed detector (flow 460 D) now misses the commonest real claim. The result schema reaches reviewers as `reviewer-finding.schema.json`, and no MANDATORY_INPUT alternative matches that name: `(?:review(?:er)?[_ -])?schema` needs `reviewer-schema` or `schema` right there, not `reviewer-finding.schema`. So `I could not read reviewer-finding.schema.json` matches neither pattern. The narrowing also dropped the round-1 fix's `does not exist`, `no such file` and `permission denied` forms, so `pr_context.json does not exist at the given path` is not caught either.
impact: A DONE reply that says it never read its result schema, or that its PR context file did not exist, counts as a complete run with scopeComplete true. That is the outcome D exists to prevent.
suggested_fix: Add `(?:[\w.-]*[_ -])?schema(?:\.json)?` (or the literal `reviewer-finding\.schema(?:\.json)?`) to MANDATORY_INPUT. Add the noun-first, sentence-anchored forms `<input> (?:does not exist|no such file|permission denied)`. Add both phrasings to the positive cases in ledger.test.ts:1147.
evidence: ledger.ts:20-37 (MANDATORY_INPUT, both UNREADABLE_INPUT patterns); ledger.test.ts:1147 positive cases name only pr_context.json, 'the result schema' and 'the context file'.

quote: return target.ref === undefined ? { error: "the package manifest records no target ref or base" } : { base: target.ref };
problem: resolveDiffBase sends every non-PR target that has no recorded base straight to `{ base: target.ref }`, and that path never runs emptyRangeWarning. For `review start --target branch --ref feat/x` (no --base), target.ref is the branch under review and target.head is the checkout HEAD (resolveTargetHead -> resolveGitHead). The recheck therefore runs `git diff feat/x...<HEAD sha>`. That range is empty when feat/x is checked out, and it is the wrong range when it is not. An empty range gives files [] and changedLines 0, which autoDepth reports as `light` (0 <= LIGHT_MAX_FILES, 0 <= LIGHT_MAX_CHANGED_LINES, no risk gate hit). The doc comment above packageDiffStats says an empty range 'is not a small diff: it refuses', but that only holds on the PR/base path.
impact: Silent wrong result. For a branch review whose dispatch says depth light, the gate accepts the light reviewer set (logic + testing + one conventions reviewer) whatever the real diff size or risk class. That is the 'one depth decision' flow 460 A set out to make trustworthy.
suggested_fix: Apply the same base resolution and empty-range refusal to non-PR targets. For kind `branch`, resolve the base the way the PR path does (recorded base, else origin/main, main, ...) and diff against it, not against the ref. Run emptyRangeWarning on every resolved base, and refuse (full set) when it fires. Only `path`/`issue`/`report` refs, which are not revisions, should fall through to the existing git-failure refusal.
evidence: src/review/coverage.ts:553-563 (resolveDiffBase: non-PR branch returns target.ref before resolveBase/emptyRangeWarning); src/commands/review.ts:1024-1048 (target {kind: branch, ref: --ref, base only from --base}); src/commands/review-plan.ts targetKindOf('feat/review-delta-rounds') === 'branch' (ref is the reviewed branch); src/review/managed.ts resolveTargetHead falls back to resolveGitHead(cwd); src/review/coverage.ts:137-156 autoDepth returns light for files [] / changedLines 0. Pre-existing in shape (main's gitDiffStats also used target.ref), but this PR rewrote the function and states the empty-range refusal as its contract.

class_scope.enumeration_method: Enumerated REVIEW_TARGET_KINDS (src/review/types.ts:29: pr, issue, branch, path, report) against resolveDiffBase. pr takes the resolveBase+emptyRangeWarning path. issue/path/report refs are URLs, paths or report labels, which fail assertGitRevision or git diff and so refuse (full). Only branch has a ref that is a valid revision equal to or near the head, so it is the one kind whose base=ref range is empty or wrong. The single site is where that branch is taken.

problem: closedAt is the newest close since `since` of any review-flow/ingest package under the chosen package's root, not of the chosen package or one this session named. Scenario: two sessions share one checkout. Session B closes its PR's package at t2. Session A's open package's manifest was last written at t1 < t2. findReviewGateState then returns null and A's gate accepts, even though A's review is not complete. The new comment narrows the release to 'the root of the package this session is on', but a sibling package closed by another session in the same root still ends this session's gate.
impact: The completion nudge is silently dropped for a review that is still open, which is the flow 460 C class (gate state taken from another run's package), now confined to one root.
suggested_fix: Count a closed package toward closedAt only when it is this session's: its dir is best.dir, or it is named by namedBySession(named, dir, [reviewId, name]), or its manifest was created since `since` by this session's pointer. Otherwise ignore it.
evidence: src/review/completion-gate.ts scanRoot records closedAt for every closed package with mtime >= since regardless of whose it is; findReviewGateState:324-325 returns null when closedAt > best.mtime. Project memory records concurrent agents sharing one checkout.

quote: Taken only from the arguments of this session's `keryx review` tool calls and from the `path:` and
problem: SessionReviewTracker.scan accepts any tool call whose arguments contain the words `keryx review` anywhere (KERYX_REVIEW_COMMAND = /\bkeryx review\b/ tested on the whole arguments string). That includes a write_file whose content mentions `keryx review`, a spawn_subagent prompt, or a grep for the phrase. Every `.metaproject/reviews/<name>` path in those arguments, and every `# managed review:` line in their output, is then recorded as named by this session. An old package referenced in such text (a prior round, a notes file) can then pass the `info.mtimeMs < since` filter in scanRoot and the non-fresh pointer check in pickPackage.
impact: Without a fresh pointer, the gate can nudge about an older package the session only mentioned in prose. That is a narrower form of the misdirection flow 460 C fixes, and it contradicts the documented 'only ... `keryx review` tool calls'.
suggested_fix: Match only shell/exec tool calls whose command starts with (or has a command segment that is) `keryx review ...`, for example by checking call.name against the shell tool and anchoring the regex to a command boundary. Alternatively, reword the doc to state the looser rule.
evidence: src/review/completion-gate.ts:106 (KERYX_REVIEW_COMMAND), :159-164 (any toolCalls entry, any tool name), :175-182 (namePaths over the whole arguments text), :99 (scanRoot admits an old package when namedBySession).

problem: The (reviewer, bare display id) fallback matches across raw files. A reviewer dispatched in several waves commonly reuses ids (raw/review-logic-w1.txt F-001 and raw/review-logic-w2.txt F-001). If the consolidated report kept the w1 finding under the bare id `F-001` and the scope-B screen removed it, the w2 raw F-001 also matches `entry.reviewer === reviewer && entry.id === fid`. This happens when w2's F-001 is not canonical (for example, the consolidator dropped it or the cap truncated it). That obligation is then closed `out-of-scope` with the w1 finding's screen reason, though no screen ever judged it.
impact: A raw finding the round lost is recorded as closed rather than surfacing as an unresolved gap, so the research ledger reads reconciled when it is not.
suggested_fix: Use the bare-id fallback only when the reviewer has exactly one raw file that reports that id. Better still, record the raw source with the screened entry and match on it.
evidence: src/review/ledger.ts:612-613 and 635-638; screenedRecord in src/review/managed.ts records only id/global_id/reviewer (no raw source), and global_id is absent at screen time because assignGlobalIds runs after the screen (managed.ts:363 vs 405).

quote: if (Array.isArray(source) && source.length > 0 && source.every((entry) => isRecord(entry) && "premises" in entry)) {
problem: When `--premises` is given two or more times, readPremises hands mergePremises an array of the parsed files. If one file lacks `premises` (for example `{judge, claims: [...]}`) the `every` test fails, and the whole array falls through to parsePremiseClaims(array). That refuses with 'must be an object `{ judge, model?, premises: [...] }`, not an array'. The refusal blames an array the CLI built, not the user's malformed file, and names neither the file nor the missing key.
impact: The ingest is still refused, so nothing is corrupted, but the operator is sent to fix the wrong thing.
suggested_fix: When source is an array of records (the multi-file shape), parse each entry with parsePremiseClaims and prefix any error with the entry's position (or file name from readPremises), so the error names the bad file and its missing `premises`.
evidence: src/commands/review.ts:3634-3641 (several files kept as an array); src/review/premise.ts parsePremiseClaims throws the not-an-array message for any non-record source.

quote: const coverage = problems.length === 0 && ctx.coverageGated ? await packageCoverageErrors(ctx.dir, dispatch) : [];
problem: Context.coverageGated says a closed package's recorded state is final and publish, the publish guard and the panel must not suddenly call it NOT READY. The flag is true for every package whose coverage.md carries COVERAGE_MD_MARK, which includes every package closed after flow 460. So for those closed packages reviewersCheck still runs packageCoverageErrors. For a light dispatch, that call re-derives the depth from live state: coverage.ts effectiveDepth runs packageDiffStats, which does a git diff of base...head at the repository top level, and then decideRoundDepth against the current project config. If the diff cannot be resolved, the depth falls back to full ('if ("error" in stats) return { depth: "full", refused: stats.error }'), and the full reviewer set then refuses the light dispatch.
impact: Trigger: a light-round PR package that closed READY after flow 460 is read again (readiness, the publish guard, the panel) in a checkout without the PR head commit, such as a fresh clone after a squash merge and branch delete. A later change to the depth thresholds or the risk-class config triggers it too. Outcome: item 3 fails with 'coverage gate (as review complete runs it): ... the diff could not be resolved', and a closed review flips to NOT READY. This is the same flip the flag was added to prevent, and the repair it names (dispatch the missing reviewers) cannot apply to a closed round.
suggested_fix: On a closed package, do not re-derive the depth from live git or config. Gate packageCoverageErrors on manifest.status !== 'closed' (open packages only), or have the closed path read the depth decision recorded at close (round-depth.json or the dispatch's own depth) instead of rechecking it. Keep the COVERAGE_MD_MARK test only for the item-6 omitted-reviewer check, which reads files and not live state.
evidence: src/review/readiness.ts:188 and :417 (coverageGated: coverageMd?.includes(COVERAGE_MD_MARK) === true || manifest.status !== "closed"). src/review/managed.ts:2736 writes COVERAGE_MD_MARK on every ingest, explicit --reviewers included, so every post-460 package carries it. src/review/coverage.ts:565-572 (diffOfTarget: git diff at gitTopLevel against resolveDiffBase, falling back to origin/main/main). src/review/coverage.ts:592-598 (effectiveDepth: a stats error, or a config decision that is not light, returns depth full). Read at head 375279e78.

class_scope.enumeration_method: Searched for every readiness consumer of coverageGated (keryx ctx rg coverageGated in src/review/readiness.ts: the item 3 gate at :188, the item 6 omitted check, and the definition at :417). Then traced packageCoverageErrors to effectiveDepth, whose two live-state inputs are the diff stats (:594) and the config depth decision (:597). The item 6 check reads only coverage.md and research.json, so it is not a member.
